title: Mirvetuximab soravtansine for FRα-positive ovarian, fallopian tube or peritoneal cancer
schedule_label: One infusion on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. The team reviews benefit and side effects each cycle. Treatment continues until the cancer progresses or side effects become unacceptable.
schedule_summary: One infusion on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. The team reviews benefit and side effects each cycle. Treatment continues until the cancer progresses or side effects become unacceptable.
purpose: The treatment aims to shrink or slow the cancer and help with symptoms. A test on the tumour shows whether enough cells have the target for this medicine.
indication_text: For adults whose high-grade serous epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer resists platinum, expresses folate receptor alpha at the required level and has had one to three prior systemic regimens.
administration_text: You receive medicines to reduce sickness and infusion reactions before the drip. The first infusion starts slowly and may speed up in steps while the nurse checks you. The dose is based on height and weight. Subsequent infusions may use the rate you previously tolerated.
monitoring_summary: Blood counts and kidney and liver tests. Review vision, breathing and sensation. New or worsening eye symptoms need an eye exam and review of the report before dosing.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Mirvetuximab soravtansine
agents.explanation: An antibody recognises folate receptor alpha on some cancer cells and carries a medicine inside them that interferes with cell division.
agents.mechanism: An antibody recognises folate receptor alpha on some cancer cells and carries a medicine inside them that interferes with cell division.
agents.watch: Call the team the same day about blurred vision, painful or light-sensitive eyes. New breathlessness or cough also needs urgent assessment.
visual: An antibody recognises folate receptor alpha on some cancer cells and carries a medicine inside them that interferes with cell division.
consent_risks: Call the same day for blurred vision, painful or very dry eyes, or sensitivity to light. Seek urgent help for sudden loss of vision.
Report new breathlessness or cough immediately. Severe breathing difficulty needs emergency help.
Tell the team about tingling, numbness, pain or trouble buttoning clothes or walking.
Tell the nurse at once about flushing, wheeze, chest tightness or faintness during the drip.

common_effects.title: What you may notice
common_effects.text: Dry eyes, blurred vision, tiredness, diarrhoea and nausea can affect usual activities. Contact the team early about any change in sight, including between infusions.

questions.a: Use the lubricating drops as advised. An eye specialist may prescribe steroid drops for subsequent cycles if the cornea shows grade 2 or worse injury. Use them only as prescribed, from infusion day through the next seven days, then wait at least 15 minutes after a steroid drop before a lubricant.

questions.q: Can I wear my contact lenses or drive home?
questions.a: Avoid contact lenses during treatment. Arrange a lift if vision changes, dizziness, numbness or tiredness affect safe driving. You can resume when symptoms have fully resolved and the team confirms it is safe.

consent_support: Discuss tumour receptor testing, the expected benefit and alternatives, injury to the eye surface, lung inflammation, nerve damage and infusion reactions. Ask about fertility and effective contraception during treatment and for 7 months after the last dose.

evidence.title: MIRASOL
evidence.interpretation: In this study about 42 in 100 people on mirvetuximab had tumour shrinkage, compared with about 16 in 100 on the chemotherapy choices. People receiving mirvetuximab lived longer as a group.
evidence.limitations: Randomised open-label trial in a biomarker-selected population. These group estimates cannot predict individual benefit or be applied to FRα-low, platinum-sensitive or differently pretreated disease.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before starting
cells: Tumour receptor test, blood count, kidney and liver tests, pregnancy test where relevant, and an eye appointment for vision and a slit-lamp examination. The team assesses nerve symptoms as indicated.
Take your glasses, eye-drop list and contact-lens details. Explain any eye disease, cough or numbness.

rows.label: Before each infusion
cells: Blood counts and kidney and liver tests. Review vision, breathing and sensation. New or worsening eye symptoms need an eye exam and review of the report before dosing.
Call promptly about blurred vision, pain, dryness or light sensitivity. The team may delay a dose to protect your eyes.

rows.label: If eye injury develops
cells: After grade 2 or worse eye toxicity, the eye team repeats exams at least every other cycle and as needed until recovery to baseline or resolution.
Use the agreed eye-drop calendar. Avoid contact lenses. Avoid driving if vision, sensation, alertness or balance is affected.

monitoring_schedule.note: The team individualises response assessments and extra tests according to symptoms and treatment aim.

additional_support: The team gives medicines before every infusion to reduce reactions and sickness. Bring your eye-drop plan and tell the nurse about any visual changes.
prescription_notes: Use all four protocol premedications once. Confirm the baseline eye examination and supply of lubricating drops.
Administer these four premedicines before each infusion. Reconcile other antiemetics and steroids with this table.

Only following a grade ≥2 infusion reaction consider additional dexamethasone 8 mg PO twice on the day before the next infusion, per prescriber. Eye steroid drops are separately prescribed by ophthalmology when indicated.
